copy_lock.copy:
More unofficial rules of marriage
that nobody tells you

Rule no. 1
“Should we order something?”
is not a question.
The decision has already been made.

Rule no. 2
If one person asks, “Kahan hai?”
The other must find it
without being told what “it” is.

Rule no. 3
Old screenshots
do not have an expiry date.
They can be presented as evidence
at any time.

Rule no. 4
The person who did not pack
will always ask,
“Charger rakh liya?”
Usually when you’re already in the cab.

Rule no. 5
Wi-Fi starts working
the moment your spouse enters the room.
Nobody knows why.

Rule no. 6
Midnight hunger
is never one person’s emergency.
The entire house gets activated.

Rule no. 7
Every unnecessary purchase
begins immediately after
a serious conversation
about saving money.

Rule no. 8
Nobody is actually in charge.
Both just keep showing up.
Usually saying, “Maine bola tha.”

agents.prompt_summary: Extract visual mechanics from references without copying frames, likenesses, or exact labels.
Prove every locked slide through concrete Aachu/Zuv behavior, not decorative illustration.
Define wants, hidden needs, eye-lines, hands, posture, distance, and joke-to-tenderness movement.
Plan readable text and brandmark placement independently for every request-locked native output.
Translate the selected visual system into specific final-generation and integrated-text constraints.
Select one system only after scoring copy alignment, relationship proof, visual variety, identity, aspect safety, and sendability.

visual_system_candidates.name: Slide-Led Evidence Plan
visual_system_candidates.case_for: Best preserves the locked copy while proving each beat through visible relationship behavior.
visual_system_candidates.risk: Must stay accountable to per-slide copy and avoid drifting into generic couple art.

visual_system_candidates.name: Format-First Label System
visual_system_candidates.case_for: Keeps the carousel visually legible and taggable when the concept depends on labels or a meme grammar.
visual_system_candidates.risk: Can become gimmicky if labels replace body language.

visual_system_candidates.name: Cinematic Romance Blocking
visual_system_candidates.case_for: Protects eye-lines, hands, distance, and emotional reversal.
visual_system_candidates.risk: Can become too soft or abstract if the hook needs deadpan specificity.

cross_debate: Keep the approved copy locked and make visuals do proof work.
Reject decorative quote-card scenes, generic couple stock poses, and repeated props.
Preserve the selected visual system unless visual-plan-quality records an explicit repair.
why_it_wins: Slide-Led Evidence Plan wins because it keeps the visual system accountable to the selected story arc.

More unofficial rules of marriage
that nobody tells you
slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Friday evening in their bedroom-living-room threshold. A half-packed suitcase is open. Aachu searches through clothes while Zuv crosses the room carrying two mugs and carefully stepping over a charging cable. They occupy different parts of the frame but exchange one familiar glance. The room is mildly unfinished, never dirty or cluttered.
slide_visual_blueprint.must_show: Visible Aachu/Zuv relationship behavior that proves the exact copy.

slide_visual_blueprint.scene: Aachu is already seated in the waiting cab with both travel bags stacked beside and across her knees. Aachu slowly turns toward him with a dry, disbelieving look; he realizes the timing and gives a sheepish half-smile. No charger appears anywhere. The joke is carried by luggage ownership, timing and reaction.

At that exact moment the router's lights become steady and the nearby laptop changes from a disconnected symbol to a simple connected symbol. Aachu slowly looks up at him, personally betrayed by technology; he gives a helpless shrug.

A folded budget note sticks harmlessly from a pocket. Both look from the object to each other with equal guilt and delight; the purchase physically requires their cooperation.
